summary: Helps implementors of IMAP4 make their software work with older IMAP2bis servers and clients. It is meant to be read alongside the earlier specification and the IMAP4 spec. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo shares compatibility advice for IMAP4 programs that encounter older IMAP2bis software. It lists feature differences but does not require implementers to support them.

questions: how to detect an old imap server
how can an imap4 client detect an older server
which imap4 commands lack imap2bis equivalents
subtitle: Compatibility notes for IMAP4 implementations that need to communicate with IMAP2bis servers or clients.

tldr.problem: IMAP2bis was common but had no definitive specification, leaving IMAP4 implementers uncertain about compatibility.
tldr.mechanism: The memo describes how to identify an IMAP2bis server and lists older commands or behaviors to use when newer IMAP4 features are missing.
tldr.outcome: The compatibility advice is informational and optional; implementers decide whether to support older software.

today: RFC 2061 is an Informational memo with no update or replacement listed in the unit metadata. It records IMAP compatibility information from December 1996.

sections.title: Why the Compatibility Notes Were Needed
sections.content:
The Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) had gone through several revisions and variants. The memo says IMAP2bis was common and widely distributed with the Pine mailer, but no definitive document described it.

This memo was intended to be read with RFC 1176 and the then-current IMAP4 specification, RFC 2060. The information is incomplete and reflects the authors' knowledge of implementations and experience. Nothing in the memo is required by IMAP4.
sections.plainLanguage: Some older mail servers were widely used even though their behavior was not fully documented. This memo shares what was known to help newer software work with them.

sections.title: IMAP4 Clients with IMAP2bis Servers
sections.content:
A client can try the CAPABILITY command. An OK reply lists supported IMAP variants; if none are recognized, the client should treat the server as IMAP2bis. A BAD reply indicates an IMAP2bis or older server.

The memo gives substitutions for missing features: use LOGIN instead of AUTHENTICATE, FIND ALL.MAILBOXES instead of LIST, and the non-extensible BODY item instead of BODYSTRUCTURE. Some facilities, including UID commands and CLOSE, have no equivalent. It also notes ambiguous IMAP2bis behavior for flags and internal dates during COPY.
sections.plainLanguage: The client can ask which features the server supports. If the server is older, the client can use several older command forms, but some newer features have no substitute.

sections.title: IMAP4 Servers with IMAP2bis Clients
sections.content:
The memo identifies one interoperability issue between an IMAP4 server and a well-written IMAP2bis client: use of a backslash in quoted strings. It recommends avoiding that case by using literals instead of quoted strings when a backslash or double quote appears in the string.

The Security Considerations section says security issues are not discussed in this memo.
sections.plainLanguage: When an older client handles quoted text with special punctuation, the memo recommends sending it as a literal instead.

references.text: RFC 1176, referenced as an IMAP specification to read alongside this memo.
RFC 2060, the then-current IMAP4 specification named in the memo.
RFC 1732, referenced for compatibility with other older IMAP variants.
